name: Corse

limits: For white wine, Vermentino: at least 75%
For white wine, Ugni Blanc: at most 25%
For white wine, Biancu Gentile, Codivarta and Genovèse together: at most 10%
For red and rosé wine, Grenache, Nielluccio and Sciaccarello together: at least 50%
For red and rosé wine, Carignan: at most 20%
For red and rosé wine, Vermentino: at most 20%
For red and rosé wine, Aleatico, Carcajolo and Morrastel together: at most 10%
rules.yield_base: 55 hl/ha for white and rosé, 45 for red

climate: Sangiovese and Grenache sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

blurb.text: A Corsican appellation for wine, with Vermentino, Grenache, Nielluccio and Sciaccarello as its main grapes. Across the island, Sangiovese covers about 29% of the vineyard area, Mammolo 26% and Vermentino 23%.
